slides.title: Family, Identity, and History
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 7 English, Unit 1: Family, Identity, and History. This is Unit 1: Family, Identity, and History. In this unit, you will explore some of the most important questions a person can ask: Where do I come from? Who are the people in my family? What stories have been passed down through the generations? You will read about families, learn how to describe your own background, and discover how people across East Africa and the wider world have moved, settled, and built new lives over the centuries. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and understand a passage about family history and migration, and discuss its ideas in English.
Use the past simple tense correctly to describe completed actions and events.
Distinguish between the past simple and the present perfect tense.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand a passage about family history and migration, and discuss its ideas in English. You will also use the past simple tense correctly to describe completed actions and events. You will also distinguish between the past simple and the present perfect tense. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: belligerent, malevolence, vindictive, infuriate, animosity, narcissistic. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Keeping the Story Alive: Oral History and Heritage
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Keeping the Story Alive: Oral History and Heritage and The Journey of Alina's Family. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: The Past Simple Tense
bullets: The past simple tense describes actions and events that started and finished in the past, which makes it the storyteller's tense. Almost every sentence in...
slides.narration: The first language focus is The Past Simple Tense. The past simple tense describes actions and events that started and finished in the past, which makes it the storyteller's tense. Almost every sentence in a biography, a family history or a chronicle depends on it, so this unit treats it as your most important tool. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Present Your Family Biography. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
